paper.title_en: <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> rotational structure in the neutron-deficient rare-earth nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Pm</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>131</mn></mmultiscripts></math>
paper.abstract_en: High-spin states in the neutron-deficient nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Pm</mi><mn>70</mn><none/><mprescripts/><mn>61</mn><mn>131</mn></mmultiscripts></math> have been investigated using the Jurogam 3 <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray spectrometer. This is the lightest promethium isotope with known excited states. The proton intruder <math><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> rotational structure has been extended to both higher and lower spin, and its unfavored-signature partner identified. This rotational structure is established down to a presumed <math><mrow><msup><mi>I</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> bandhead of the <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mspace width="0.16em"/><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>532</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> Nilsson orbital, which is also expected to form the ground state of this deformed nucleus. Systematic comparisons are made with cranked shell-model calculations.
